corpus_definition: A general word for objects or things.

forms.definition: things, or a group of things, when you do not say their names
forms.example: Please take your stuff off the table.

syn.note: Same meaning; a little less informal.
The things that a person owns.

forms.definition: to push things into a space quickly and carelessly
forms.example: He stuffed his clothes into the bag.

syn.note: Push too many things into a small space.

forms.definition: completely full, often of food you have eaten
forms.example: I ate three plates of plov and now I am stuffed.

forms.definition: (of a room) hot and without fresh air
forms.example: Open the window, it is stuffy in here.
forms.note: Belongs to stuff = block up, not things.

context.text: Aziz had too much stuff for one small bag. He stuffed it all in anyway.

corpus_definition: a particular way of doing or making something

forms.definition: a particular way of doing, making or wearing something
forms.example: That dress is a very popular style this year.

syn.note: A style that is popular at one time.
The way something is planned and made.

forms.definition: a person whose job is cutting hair or choosing clothes for people
forms.example: My sister works as a stylist in a salon.

forms.definition: to shape hair or design clothes in a particular way
forms.example: She styled her hair for the wedding.

syn.note: Put into a nice shape or order.

forms.definition: fashionable and attractive
forms.example: He wears very stylish shoes.

forms.definition: in a fashionable and attractive way
forms.example: She was stylishly dressed for the party.

context.text: Malika has her own style. She always looks stylish, even in simple clothes.

corpus_definition: to pull liquid or air into your mouth using your lips

forms.definition: the act of pulling liquid or air into your mouth
forms.example: The child took a long suck on the straw.

forms.definition: to pull liquid or air into your mouth with your lips
forms.example: The baby sucks milk from the bottle.

ant.note: Push air out of your mouth.

context.text: The baby sucks her thumb when she is tired. After one long suck she falls asleep.

reviewer_note: sucker is informal (easily tricked); placed as other_meaning.

corpus_definition: to be right or good for someone

forms.definition: how right or good something is for a person or purpose
forms.example: We checked the suitability of the room for the class.

forms.definition: to look good on someone, or be right for them
forms.example: That colour does not really suit you.

syn.note: Be the right size or shape.

forms.definition: right or good for a particular person or purpose
forms.example: This film is not suitable for children.

ant.note: Not right for someone or something.

forms.definition: in a way that is right for the situation
forms.example: He was suitably dressed for the interview.

context.text: This job suits Sardor well. It is suitable for someone who likes people.

reviewer_note: Clothes sense is a separate map.

corpus_definition: matching jacket and trousers worn for formal business or events

forms.definition: a jacket and trousers or skirt made of the same cloth
forms.example: He wore a blue suit to the meeting.

syn.note: A set of clothes worn together.

forms.note: Verb suit (be right for) is the other map.

forms.definition: wearing a suit
forms.example: Two suited men waited at the door.

context.text: My father bought a new suit for my brother's wedding. All the suited guests looked very smart.

reviewer_note: Separate map from suit = be right for.

corpus_definition: To help or encourage someone you like.

forms.definition: help and kind words that you give someone
forms.example: Thank you for your support during my exams.

syn.note: General word for doing things for someone.

forms.definition: to help and encourage someone
forms.example: My family will support me in my new job.

syn.note: Do things to make something easier for someone.
Give someone confidence to do something.
Say you agree with and help someone.

forms.definition: giving help and kind words
forms.example: My teacher was very supportive when I was ill.

people.definition: a person who helps someone or likes a sports team
people.example: He is a big supporter of Pakhtakor football club.

context.text: Dilnoza's parents support her dream of studying abroad. They are very supportive.

corpus_definition: salty liquid that comes out of your skin when hot or nervous

forms.definition: salty liquid that comes out of your skin when you are hot
forms.example: Sweat dripped down his face after the run.

forms.definition: to produce salty liquid on your skin because you are hot or nervous
forms.example: I always sweat a lot in summer.

forms.definition: wet with salty liquid from your skin
forms.example: My shirt was sweaty after football.

people.definition: a warm piece of clothing for the top of your body
people.example: Wear a sweater, it is cold.
people.note: Now just means a jumper, not something linked to body liquid.

context.text: In July in Tashkent you sweat even in the shade. Everyone on the bus is sweaty.

reviewer_note: sweater is historically related but means jumper.

corpus_definition: To clean a floor using a long brush.

forms.definition: the act of cleaning a floor with a long brush
forms.example: The kitchen needs a good sweep.

forms.definition: to clean a floor using a long brush
forms.example: I need to sweep the kitchen floor today.

forms.definition: affecting many things or people
forms.example: The government made sweeping changes.
forms.note: Belongs to sweep = move over a large area, not cleaning.

people.definition: a person or machine that cleans floors or streets
people.example: The street sweeper starts work at five in the morning.

context.text: Grandma sweeps the yard every morning. Yesterday she swept it twice because of the wind.

corpus_definition: to move back and forth; also a seat hanging on ropes for children

forms.definition: a seat hanging on ropes that children move back and forth on
forms.example: There are two swings in the park.

forms.definition: to move backwards and forwards while hanging from something
forms.example: The children loved to swing in the park.

syn.note: Move slowly from side to side.

context.text: My little brother swings on the swing for hours. Yesterday he swung so high he laughed and shouted.

reviewer_note: Noun swing (seat) covered by corpus definition too.

corpus_definition: To complete a test to show your knowledge.
usage_note: British English uses 'take' or 'sit' an exam; 'pass' means you were successful, 'fail' means you were not. Do not say 'make an exam'.

context.text: Kamola will take an exam in English tomorrow. She took an exam last year too and passed.

reviewer_note: 'make an exam' is a common learner error.

corpus_definition: To join an activity or event with others.
usage_note: Always followed by a noun or -ing form: 'take part in the race', 'take part in singing'. Not 'take part on'.

relations.note: Start doing an activity with others.
Take part in a race or competition.

context.text: Will you take part in the school competition? Last year twenty students took part in it.
